**Proof.**

Let $(X_t)_{t \geq 0}$ be a continuous-time $L^2$-martingale, i.e. an adapted process on a filtered probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, (\mathcal{F}_t)_{t\geq 0}, \mathbb{P})$ satisfying the martingale property and with $\mathbb{E}[X_t^2] < \infty$ for every $t \geq 0$.

We must show that $\mathbb{E}|X_t| < \infty$ for every $t \geq 0$.

Fix an arbitrary $t \geq 0$. By hypothesis $X_t \in L^2(\Omega, \mathcal{F}_t, \mathbb{P})$, i.e. $\mathbb{E}[X_t^2] < \infty$.

Since $X_t$ is a real-valued random variable, $|X_t|^2 = X_t^2$. Applying the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality to the pair $(|X_t|, \mathbf{1})$ gives

$$
\mathbb{E}|X_t| \;=\; \mathbb{E}\big[|X_t|\cdot \mathbf{1}\big] \;\leq\; \big(\mathbb{E}[|X_t|^2]\big)^{1/2}\big(\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{1}^2]\big)^{1/2} \;=\; \big(\mathbb{E}[X_t^2]\big)^{1/2}.
$$

(Equivalently, this is the standard inclusion $L^2 \subseteq L^1$ on a probability space, obtained from Jensen's inequality applied to the convex function $x \mapsto x^2$ together with $|x| \leq 1 + x^2$, or directly from Cauchy–Schwarz as above.)

Since $\mathbb{E}[X_t^2] < \infty$ by assumption, the right-hand side is finite, hence

$$
\mathbb{E}|X_t| \leq \big(\mathbb{E}[X_t^2]\big)^{1/2} < \infty.
$$

Because $t \geq 0$ was arbitrary, $\mathbb{E}|X_t| < \infty$ holds for all $t \geq 0$.

Therefore every continuous-time $L^2$-martingale (with $\mathbb{E}[X_t^2] < \infty$ for all $t$) automatically satisfies the integrability condition $\mathbb{E}|X_t| < \infty$ for all $t$, and so is a martingale in the usual ($L^1$) sense as well. $\blacksquare$

### PROOF COMPLETE
